_note: Reference events used ONLY for historical context in advisories. Figures are approximate published estimates from news and official reporting, not precise official statistics, and are shown to convey scale. Matching is threshold-based (see `criteria`), never impressionistic, and a match is never presented as a prediction.

events.name: June 2025 Assam floods
events.summary: Sustained pre-monsoon and early monsoon rainfall across the Brahmaputra basin flooded large parts of Assam, affecting more than 600,000 people across multiple districts.
events.headline_fact: more than 600,000 people were affected across Assam
events.source_note: Approximate figure from contemporaneous reporting on the June 2025 Assam flood situation.

events.name: August 2018 Kerala floods
events.summary: Kerala received far above-normal monsoon rainfall and every major dam was opened, producing the state's worst flooding in close to a century.
events.headline_fact: around 5.4 million people were affected and over 480 lives were lost
events.source_note: Figures from Kerala State Disaster Management Authority and central government reporting on the 2018 floods.

events.name: Cyclone Amphan
events.summary: A super cyclonic storm made landfall near the West Bengal-Bangladesh border with extremely destructive winds and a large storm surge.
events.headline_fact: sustained winds near 155 km/h damaged large parts of coastal West Bengal
events.source_note: Wind figures from India Meteorological Department bulletins issued during Cyclone Amphan.
events.source: India Meteorological Department — RSMC New Delhi

events.name: December 2015 Chennai floods
events.summary: An exceptionally wet north-east monsoon culminated in extreme rainfall that overwhelmed the Adyar and Cooum basins and inundated much of the city.
events.headline_fact: close to 490 mm of rain fell in a single day on 1 December 2015
events.source_note: Rainfall figure from India Meteorological Department records for the December 2015 Chennai event.

events.name: The 26 July 2005 Mumbai deluge
events.summary: An intense mesoscale system stalled over Mumbai and produced one of the highest single-day rainfall totals ever recorded in an Indian city.
events.headline_fact: 944 mm of rain fell over Santacruz in 24 hours
events.source_note: Rainfall figure from the India Meteorological Department Santacruz observatory record for 26 July 2005.
